Immersive experience · 2022

Financial
Adventure

A mobile museum tour where younger visitors learn about finance through agent missions and interactive exhibits.

RoleProduct Designer
ScopeInteraction design, visual design, user flows, prototyping
ClientFinancial Explorer 62 · Taiwan Academy of Banking and Finance
TimelineJune–December 2022

The brief

Younger visitors showed little interest in the financial museum, and they did not always leave with a clear sense of what they had learned. The brief was to make the museum’s content more engaging and give younger audiences a reason to explore.

As the product designer, I planned the visitor experience for a new mobile-guided tour and defined the design direction. My work covered interaction design, visual design, user flows, and prototyping.

Working with the existing museum

We had to introduce a new experience without changing the existing equipment or getting in the way of the museum’s exhibits. Groups needed to move through the space without crossing paths or crowding around the same activity.

The experience also spanned several physical and digital touchpoints. Our goal was to connect them into a continuous story, using a mobile guide and interactive tasks to encourage visitors to explore financial concepts.

Planning the route

We reviewed the gallery layout and exhibit content to find suitable places for activities. The space formed a loop, with each area focused on one topic.

We placed activities in wider areas and avoided corners where groups could gather. From the entrance, visitors would turn left and follow the gallery in one direction to reduce conflicts between groups.

Understanding younger visitors

We used questionnaires and semi-structured interviews to explore how our target audience felt about finance, what brought them to museums, and the kinds of experiences they enjoyed.

Participants were unfamiliar with financial concepts and the financial industry. Their limited use of financial services also gave them fewer reasons to take an interest.

They described traditional museum learning as dull and wanted to share the experience with friends. These findings helped us focus on a story visitors could take part in together.

An agent mission in five stages

Through a series of ideation sessions, we developed a story in which visitors became agents. Each task and puzzle introduced financial knowledge while giving them a reason to continue.

The journey had five stages: introduction, intelligence gathering, suspect identification, code breaking, and a final financial defense challenge.

From visitor flow to prototype

I mapped the experience across five stages and 58 interface screens. The interface was inspired by an agent’s pager, connecting the on-screen tasks with the role visitors were playing.

We used low-fidelity prototypes based on the user flow for internal usability testing and system integration. A lightweight handheld device and a custom wrist holder supported the activities and reinforced the agent role.

Designing the visual language

The visual direction drew on mystery and gaming references to attract visitors’ attention.

I added subtle noise to the logo to give it a mysterious feel. The palette drew on cyberpunk and utopian references: gold connected to the financial theme, while silver-white lines suggested technology.

Fragmented graphics and fluorescent highlights helped important information stand out.

Bringing the story into the gallery

Storytelling

The sign-in sequence revealed the visitor’s agent identity and gave the experience a memorable start.

Interactive experience

Interactive puzzles connected instructions on the device with the physical exhibits. The experience used multiple devices and included tasks that encouraged visitors to cooperate or compete with their companions. A team progress display showed how the group was doing.

Visitor response

The tour launched at Financial Explorer 62. The museum’s management team and younger visitors responded positively. It received more than 4,000 bookings in its first year.

Average score in a user-testing questionnaire

9.4 / 10

Most respondents said the interactive format made financial topics more interesting and challenged their expectations of a dull museum visit.
